image.subject: 達美航空 DL1181 班機於紐約拉瓜地亞機場重飛發生機尾擦地事故 NTSB發布初步調查

zh.title: 達美航空 DL1181 班機於紐約拉瓜地亞機場重飛發生機尾擦地事故 NTSB發布初步調查
zh.summary: 達美DL1181在拉瓜地亞重飛時機尾擦地；NTSB發布初步調查
body: 7月14日，美國達美航空（Delta Air Lines）一架機身編號 N382DN 的空中巴士 A321-200 客機，執行由佛羅里達州勞德岱堡-好萊塢國際機場（FLL）飛往紐約拉瓜地亞機場（LGA）的 DL1181 航班時，於降落過程中發生機尾擦地（Tail strike）事故。該班機在準備降落於第 22 號跑道的最後進場階段，機組人員執行了重飛（Go-around）程序，在此期間機身尾段與跑道表面發生接觸。 事故發生後，機組人員隨即將客機拉升至約 4,000 呎的安全高度進行盤旋與處置，並在約 13 分鐘後重新進場，順利且安全地降落。根據初步通報，機上所有乘客與機組人員均未在此次事件中受傷。 此次涉事的空中巴士 A321-200 為 A320 家族中機身最長的型號。由於其修長的機體設計，在起飛、降落或執行重飛階段，若機首俯仰角（Pitch attitude）控制過大，相對其他短機身型號更容易產生機尾觸地的風險。此外，拉瓜地亞機場因腹地較小，且第 22 號跑道長度有限，對飛行員的進場精準度要求極高，在重飛等高工作負載（High workload）的動態環境下，更考驗對操作細節的掌握。 美國國家運輸安全委員會（NTSB）已將本案正式定義為「事故」（Accident），並指出該客機的機體尾段在此次接觸中受到了「實質性損害」（Substantial damage）。NTSB 已於 2026 年 7 月 29 日發布初步調查訊息，目前正持續針對事發當時的標準操作程序、飛行數據以及潛在的人為因素進行綜合分析，以釐清確切的肇因與完整經過。

en.title: Delta Air Lines Flight DL1181 Tail Strike During Go-Around at New York LaGuardia; NTSB Issues Preliminary Investigation
en.summary: Delta DL1181 suffers LaGuardia tail strike during go-around; NTSB opens preliminary investigation
body: On July 14, 2026, a Delta Air Lines Airbus A321-200 (registration N382DN) operating flight DL1181 from Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL) to New York LaGuardia Airport (LGA) experienced a tail strike during landing. While on final approach to Runway 22, the crew initiated a go-around, during which the aircraft's tail contacted the runway surface. Following the occurrence, the crew climbed the aircraft to a safe altitude of about 4,000 feet to hold and assess the situation, and approximately 13 minutes later conducted a new approach, landing smoothly and safely. According to the preliminary report, all passengers and crew on board were uninjured. The involved Airbus A321-200 is the longest-fuselage variant in the A320 family; its elongated design makes it more susceptible than shorter variants to tail contact if the pitch attitude is excessively high during takeoff, landing, or go-around. Additionally, LaGuardia Airport's constrained surroundings and the limited length of Runway 22 demand high approach precision, and the dynamic, high-workload environment of a go-around further tests pilots' handling of operational details. The U.S. National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has officially classified the event as an 'accident' and noted that the aircraft's tail section sustained 'substantial damage' from the contact. The NTSB issued a preliminary investigation notice on July 29, 2026, and is continuing a comprehensive analysis of the standard operating procedures, flight data, and potential human factors at the time of the occurrence to determine the exact cause and full sequence of events.
